pinterest.title: Engagement Ring Insurance: How to Protect Your Ring at Home and Abroad
pinterest.description: Engagement ring insurance is not automatic. A contents policy can cover jewellery, but per-item limits mean you may need to add the ring and check its value. Travel insurance often caps each valuable and rarely pays for unattended items, so it is not a substitute. Our general information guide covers the three ways to insure a ring, what to check in a PDS and how to carry it on a proposal or wedding abroad.

pinterest.title: How to Insure an Engagement Ring: Questions to Ask Before You Rely on a Policy
pinterest.description: Before you rely on any policy for your engagement ring, ask: is loss covered as well as theft and damage? Does cover apply overseas, and for how long? Is it agreed, market or replacement value? Repair, replace or cash? What conditions apply to unattended items and luggage? When does cover start? Save this checklist and read it against the PDS. General information only, not financial advice.

pinterest.title: Travelling With Your Rings to a Destination Wedding: Engagement Ring Insurance Tips
pinterest.description: Three rings usually travel to a destination wedding. Pack them in your carry-on, tell your insurer your travel dates and keep them on a hand or in the room safe. Standard travel policies typically exclude items left unattended, items not in an available hotel safe and theft from checked baggage. On pool and boat days, swap to a plain band. If a ring is stolen, report it to local police first.

slides: Is your engagement ring actually insured? It is not automatic.
Three places a ring can sit: your home contents policy, a separate policy for valuables, or travel insurance while you are away.
Contents cover can include jewellery, but most policies cap what you can claim per item. You may need to add the ring with its own value.
Travel insurance is not a substitute. It often caps each valuable and typically excludes unattended items and theft from checked baggage.
Questions for your insurer: loss as well as theft? Overseas cover? Agreed, market or replacement value? Repair, replace or cash? When does cover start?
Keep the kit together: receipt, grading report, valuation and photos. Note any laser inscription and revalue about every two years.
Flying to propose or to the wedding? Rings go in your carry-on, tell your insurer your travel dates, and use the room safe.
